subject: Post-call: SDK/auth routing and observability hooks for Orchid Analytics integration

Subject: Post-call: SDK/auth routing and observability hooks for Orchid Analytics integration

Thanks again for the call earlier — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have shared alignment on the integration surface and observability expectations.

Recap (technical highlights)
- SDK: you want a lightweight Python/Node SDK to be the primary integration path; plan to host client in your infra behind your proxy.
- Auth: primary preference is API-key scoped to workspace; Kate mentioned potential mTLS for high-security endpoints for PII workloads.
- Routing & fallbacks: route by latency SLO (US primary, EU fallback), with an automatic fallback to a quantized cheaper model when load spikes.
- Structured output/tool calling: Orchid wants structured JSON outputs (tool-calls) to drive downstream extraction; we should validate schemas server-side.
- Embeddings/rerank: initial plan is embeddings for semantic search + a small reranker (cross-encoder) for top-k results. Data will be sent via your ingestion pipeline, not stored in Redwood.
- Observability: you need a per-request trace id propagated through SDK and into Redwood logs. Desired telemetry: request_id, trace_id, model, model_version, input_tokens, output_tokens, total_latency_ms, decode_latency_ms, kernel_latency_ms. Also want a latency-breakdown header in responses for dashboarding.

Open items / asks from Orchid
1) Alex: sample SDK call showing how to attach a trace header and how the response headers look.
2) Kate: guidance on auth choices (API key vs mTLS) and migration path if you enable mTLS later.
3) Both: recommended config for embeddings indexing (dimension, quantization) and expected tokenization differences.

Proposed next steps
- I will share a short SDK example + a minimal observability spec by EOD tomorrow (attached).
- Rishi (SE) will join a technical workshop to review routing/fallback policies and embeddings tuning — can we target a 60-minute deep-dive next week?
- Kate/Alex: please share a short sample corpus (2-3 documents) and target queries so Rishi can build a repro.

Thanks,

Thanks Jordan — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we schedule the workshop: 

- Trace propagation: are you proposing a custom header (e.g., X-Request-Trace) or using W3C traceparent? We prefer W3C if possible to keep our tracing consistent.
- Response headers: can the latency breakdown be returned both as headers and in the JSON body? We want per-request spikes surfaced in logs and also top-line metrics in the dashboard.
- Auth: we need a concrete fallback/migration path if we start with API keys and later enable mTLS. Does Redwood support dual-mode auth?
- Data handling: you said data is not stored by default — can you confirm retention/retention override policies for embeddings? We will need this for procurement/security review.

If those answers look good we can move to schedule next week's technical workshop. I can bring our infra lead (SRE) if needed.

—Alex

Forwarding with SE notes and attachments. I attached a short SDK example and an observability fields matrix. Key notes for the workshop: 

1) Trace header recommendations
- We support W3C traceparent out of the box. For backwards compatibility we also accept X-Request-Trace. Example: 
  - W3C: traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
  - Redwood header: X-Request-Trace: rwd-20260212-9f8b7c6

2) Response latency breakdown (headers + body)
- We can return both. Headers: X-Total-Latency-ms, X-Decode-Latency-ms, X-Kernel-Latency-ms. Body field: "latency_breakdown": {"total_ms":123, "decode_ms":34, "kernel_ms":45}. The SDK will surface both to the app and push to traces.

3) Auth migration path
- Dual-mode: start with API keys; when you enable mTLS we support client certs at the TLS layer plus short-lived tokens for per-request auth. We'll provide rollout ops: (1) enable mTLS on a staging route, (2) run a probe to verify client cert mapping, (3) rotate keys after a successful cutover.

4) Embeddings/re-ranker guidance
- Default embedding dim: 768 or 1024 depending on model; recommend 768 for initial index. Quantization: int8 for storage, but run nearest-neighbor with a small PQ bucket for fast kNN. We'll share a short eval script for recall vs latency.

Attachments (in thread):
- redwood_sdk_example.py (contains sample trace propagation + header parsing + response latency teardown)
- orchid_integration_flow.drawio.png (architecture diagram)
- observability_fields.csv (matrix with field names and types)

Small inline snippet (from redwood_sdk_example.py):

# send request with trace header
headers = {
    "traceparent": traceparent,
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}",
}
resp = requests.post(endpoint, headers=headers, json=payload)
print(resp.headers.get("X-Total-Latency-ms"), resp.json().get("latency_breakdown"))

I'll prep a short agenda for the 60-minute workshop: 10m setup, 20m SDK/auth, 20m embeddings + reranker, 10m observability + Q&A.

—Rishi
